claim: Inference: Italy (FL Europe's largest market, ~154 of 559 stores = ~27%) has been roughly flat since the deal, with net post-deal closures of about 0-3 and the rest relocations. So most of the ~22 European closures since 9/2025 sit outside Italy, implying an ex-Italy closure rate of roughly 5-7%/yr against the ~4%/yr headline.
data_point: Italy now 154 (two sources) vs 'circa 160' FY24 / 'circa 150' May-2025. Post-deal Italy changes found are mostly relocations: Giugliano 06338->06438, Arese 06402->06452, Taranto 06342->06532, Quartucciu 06500->06560, Bolzano ->06400. Ex-Italy math: ~19-21 of 22 closures over ~405 stores in ~9 months = ~6-7%/yr. Worst case (all 6 Italy net closures post-deal): 16/~420 = ~5%/yr, still above 4%.
source_name: Computed: careers feed + stores.footlocker.it sitemap + Wayback locator diff + retail&food / Borsa&Finanza counts
verifier_note: Labelled inference. Inputs verified: both 154 counts and the relocation pairs. The Wayback diff (147 of ~160 IDs, partial coverage) was not independently re-run. The Italy count at deal close is not directly observed. The directional conclusion (ex-Italy rate > 4%/yr headline) holds even in the worst case, at ~5%/yr.
